source.title: Open Problems: Matrix Hamiltonians with a chance of being complex symmetric

accepted.question_text: Consider the finite-dimensional PT-symmetric real matrix Hamiltonians H(N) satisfying H = P H^† P = H^†, with matrix dimension N and, when N = 2J or N = 2J + 1, depending on a J-tuple of real couplings g1, g2, ..., gJ. Their spectrum is real and therefore observable only for couplings inside a stability domain D; on the boundary ∂D, formed by Kato exceptional points, the matrices become similar to matrices containing Jordan blocks. Determine whether, in a neighborhood of ∂D, one can explicitly represent this family in a form that is complex symmetric, equivalently by giving an explicit isospectral mapping from these special real matrices to suitable complex symmetric counterparts.
accepted.context_brief: PT-symmetric matrix Hamiltonians near exceptional-point boundary

evidence.quote: Abstract. An explicit form of an isospectral mapping is sought between given, special real matrices and their arbitrary suitable complex symmetric avatars.

Question. PT-symmetric matrix Hamiltonians H = PH†P = H†, viz., H(N) = ... have the spectrum which only remains real and observable inside a domain D of couplings. On the boundary ∂D of stability (formed by Kato’s exceptional points) these matrices are similar to ones containing Jordan blocks. In some vicinity of ∂D one could try to find the form of these matrices which would be complex symmetric.
A few comments. At dimensions N = 2J or N = 2J + 1 these models depend just on a J-plet of real couplings g1, g2, ..., gJ.
